test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 30 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the INCORRECT statement related to tropism.

options.text: Geotropism — in response to the pull of earth or gravity

solution:
The Correct answer is __**Phototropism — movement towards water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Phototropism** refers to the **movement or growth of plants in response to light.**
 
• It is a directional movement where the plant grows **towards the light source** (positive phototropism) or away from it (negative phototropism).
 
• The hormone responsible for phototropism is **auxin,** which facilitates growth on the side of the plant away from the light.
 
• Phototropism ensures that plants optimize the absorption of **light for photosynthesis.**
 
• The statement “movement towards water” is incorrect because phototropism is specifically related to **light stimuli**, not water.
 
• Water stimuli lead to **hydrotropism,** which is another form of tropism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chemotropism — movement towards chemical**__

 __
 
• **Chemotropism** refers to the **growth or movement of plants** in response to a chemical stimulus.
 
• Examples include the **growth of pollen tubes towards ovules** during fertilization in plants.
 
• This type of tropism helps plants in important processes such as **reproduction.**
 
 
 
• **Hydrotropism — movement towards water**__
 __
 
• **Hydrotropism** is the **movement or growth of plant roots** towards a water source.
 
• It ensures that plant roots can access **adequate water** for survival and growth.
 
• This type of tropism is crucial for plants thriving in **dry or arid conditions.**
 
 
 
• **Geotropism — in response to the pull of earth or gravity**__
 
 
• **Geotropism** refers to the **growth or movement of plants** in response to gravity.
 
• Plant roots exhibit **positive geotropism** by growing downward into the soil.
 
• Plant shoots exhibit **negative geotropism** by growing upward away from the gravitational pull.
 
• This type of tropism helps plants maintain proper **structural orientation.**
